title: The Quiet Hours
author: Suraj
shortDescription: Poems for the hour after everyone has gone to sleep.
description:
A collection of short poems about solitude that does not feel lonely. Written between midnight and morning, The Quiet Hours is for anyone learning to sit with themselves.

Each poem fits on a single page, so the book can be opened anywhere and still make sense.
excerpt:
The kettle clicks off.
The house breathes out.

I used to fill this silence
with somebody else's noise.
Tonight I let it stay,
and it turns out to be company.

title: Soft Return
author: Suraj
shortDescription: Love poems about coming back, gently.
description: Soft Return follows one love story from the first message to the long, patient middle. It is about choosing someone again on the ordinary Tuesdays.
excerpt:
You do not arrive like thunder.
You arrive like the light
that was always on in the hallway,
so I never had to ask
whether I was welcome.

title: The Long Way Home
author: Suraj
shortDescription: Essays on leaving, wandering and finding your own front door.
description: Twelve short essays about the detours that taught the author who they were. Equal parts travel diary and conversation with a friend.
excerpt:
Everyone gave me directions.
Nobody mentioned that home
is not a place you reach,
but a way of walking
you slowly learn.

title: Small Mercies
author: Suraj
shortDescription: Tiny stories about the kindness nobody notices.
description: Small Mercies collects fifty-two very short stories — one for every week — about strangers, neighbours and the small acts that quietly hold a day together.
excerpt:
The tea seller added extra sugar
without being asked.
I had not told him
it was my father's birthday
and I was far from home.

title: Letters to Someone Kind
author: Suraj
shortDescription: Unsent letters, written with a full heart.
description: A book of letters addressed to no one in particular and everyone who needed them: to a younger self, a friend who moved away, a love that ended well.
excerpt:
Dear you,
I hope someone is
reminding you to eat,
to rest, to laugh
at the wrong moment.
I would, if I were there.

title: Unlearning
author: Suraj
shortDescription: A year of letting go of what was never yours.
description: Unlearning is a year-long notebook of reflections on perfectionism, comparison and rest. Short entries, honest questions, and room to write back.
excerpt:
I was taught to be impressive.
Nobody taught me to be at ease.
This year I am practising
the second one.
